MUJAHID:v2p577#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p577#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p577#2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses having no refuge on that day as having no shelter or protection.

MUJAHID:v2p577#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p577#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p577#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses having no one to defend you as having no helper to support you.

MUQATIL:42:46-49/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:46-49/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:46-49/r2.claim: People should answer their Lord in faith and monotheism before the irreversible Day comes; then there will be no shelter or escape from punishment.

TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r1.claim: God's disbelieving enemies will have no protectors to prevent their punishment; whoever God misguides has no path to guidance, which belongs to God alone.

TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r2.claim: People must answer God's call by believing and following his messenger before the unpreventable Day of Resurrection comes.

TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r3.claim: On that day people will have no stronghold or refuge from the punishment brought by their disbelief.

TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r4.claim: They will be unable to change the punishment or retaliate against God when he punishes them.

TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses refuge as a place of protection and “nakīr” as a helper who can aid them.

TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p534#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī glosses refuge as a place to shelter and “nakīr” as strength or honor in which they could take pride.

ZAJJAJ:v4p401#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p401#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p401#2/r3.claim: There is no refuge from punishment, and people will be unable to deny their sins or the punishment that comes upon them.

NAHHAS:v4p90/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p90/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p90/r5.claim: Min maljaʾ means ‘any refuge’; people must not deny what has been laid before them of their deeds.

SULAMI:v2p229#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p229#4/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p229#4/r1.claim: God's response is for the one who hears His inner calls, commands, and address; without hearing, a person has no place from which to answer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r1.claim: A refuge means a place of escape or protected haven.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r2.claim: There will be no secure shelter.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r3.claim: There will be no helper to support them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r4.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p210/r4.claim: Alternatively, no denier can alter what has befallen them.

QUSHAYRI:v3p169/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p169/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p169/r1.claim: Responding to God means keeping His covenant, fulfilling His due, turning from disobedience to companionship, and submitting to His decree; the path is open now but will close suddenly.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:47/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:47/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:47/r1.claim: Respond to God with faith and obedience before the irreversible Day; then there will be no escape from punishment and no ability to deny or change what befalls you.

JISHUMI:v9p6266#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6266#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6266#2/r2.claim: A maljaʾ is a place to which one flees for refuge.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p199#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p199#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p199#2/r2.claim: Responding to the Lord means answering His caller, Muhammad.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p199#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p199#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p199#2/r3.claim: The Day of Resurrection cannot be repelled; no refuge or denier can change what happens.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p42/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p42/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p42/r2.claim: People must answer God's call before Resurrection, which cannot be reversed to allow further action; they will have no refuge or escape except through knowing God and doing good beforehand.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p42/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p42/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p42/r3.claim: Nakīr is a verbal noun for denial, like other verbal nouns, or possibly an active participle from nakira, though that sense is semantically remote.

TABRISI:42:46-50/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:46-50/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:46-50/r1.claim: People are urged to answer their Lord’s call through Muhammad and submit to obedience before a day that cannot be returned from; the day may be Judgment, which no one can repel, or death, which cannot be delayed.

TABRISI:42:46-50/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:46-50/r2.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:42:46-50/r2.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī identifies the day as Judgment, after which no one can return to the world and which no one can repel.

TABRISI:42:46-50/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:46-50/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:42:46-50/r3.claim: Abu Muslim identifies the day as death, which cannot be turned aside or postponed from its appointed time.

TABRISI:42:46-50/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:46-50/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:46-50/r4.claim: On that day there is no refuge from punishment and no way to deny or alter it; another explanation of nakīr is a helper who would deny what befalls them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p295/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p295/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p295/r1.claim: Respond to your Lord by answering His call through His messenger before Resurrection Day, which no one can avert or repel.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p295/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p295/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p295/r2.claim: No refuge means there is no helper who can aid them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p295/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p295/r3.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p295/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that they will have no ability to alter what has happened to them.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r1.claim: Respond to the Lord by accepting His call to faith and obedience.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r2.claim: The day that cannot be repelled is Resurrection; no one can turn it back once God has ordained its time.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r3.claim: There will be no refuge to save people from punishment.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r4.claim: Mujāhid interprets the lack of a nakīr as having no helper to support them.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r5.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī takes nakīr as the punishment that will come to them, with the word meaning something painful or causing pain.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r6.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj says they will not be able to deny the sins brought before them.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:47/r7.claim: Nakīr may mean denial of the punishment or the act of changing what is objectionable; the punishment cannot be denied.

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:46-48/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:46-48/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:46-48/r2.claim: Respond before the irreversible Day: God will not reverse His decree; alternatively, من attaches to يأتي, describing a Day from God that cannot be repelled.

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:46-48/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:46-48/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:46-48/r3.claim: There will be no refuge and no denial of past deeds, since they are recorded and testified to by tongues and limbs.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p106#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p106#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p106#5/r1.claim: Respond to God's call before the Day of Resurrection, which God cannot reverse after decreeing it; the phrase may modify “no reversal” or “a day comes from God.”

NASAFI-FULL:v4p106#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p106#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p106#5/r2.claim: On that day there is no refuge from punishment and no ability to deny anything recorded among one's deeds.

SAMIN-DURR:42:47/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:47/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:47/r1.claim: من الله may modify يأتي, meaning a day that comes from God, or an omitted clause explaining that the day cannot be averted from what God decrees.

SAMIN-DURR:42:47/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:47/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:42:47/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches من الله to لا مرد.

SAMIN-DURR:42:47/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:47/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:42:47/r3.claim: The Shaykh objects that this makes the phrase extended, which should be accusative and without tanwin.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p215#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p215#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p215#2/r1.claim: People must answer their Lord before the irreversible Day, which occurs instantly when God commands and has no preventer.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p215#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p215#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p215#2/r2.claim: No fortress or hiding place can conceal anyone from God's knowledge, sight, and power; there is no refuge except in Him, as 75:10–12 says.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r1.claim: There is no escape from error or the punishment it causes; therefore people must answer their Lord's call through the Messenger's commands.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r2.claim: They must respond before the irreversible Day arrives; even a small act of good before death makes timely obedience urgent.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r3.claim: No one can reverse that Day because it comes from God, who possesses all majesty and whose decision none can overturn.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p646/r4.claim: On that Day there will be no refuge or fortress and no one can deny people's acts to rescue them: recorders and their own limbs will testify.

DURR-FULL:v7p361/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p361/r3.speaker: زيد بن صوحان
DURR-FULL:v7p361/r3.claim: When Zayd ibn Suhan recited the command to respond to God before the unavoidable day, he answered, ‘Here I am, Zayd.’

DURR-FULL:v7p361/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p361/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p361/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses a refuge as a place of protection and ‘no denier’ as no helper who can help them.

BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r1.claim: People must answer their Lord’s call to faith, conveyed through His Prophet, before the day decreed by God arrives and cannot be turned back.

BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r10.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r10.claim: The way to answer remains open now, but will suddenly close to hearts when the appointed day arrives.

BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r2.claim: ‘From God’ may qualify ‘repelled,’ meaning God will not reverse His decree, or it may mean a day coming from God that cannot be repelled.

BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r3.claim: Sa‘di’s marginal commentary notes a rhetorical nuance in addressing God as Lord, denying any return, and using the comprehensive divine name.

BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r4.claim: There will be no refuge or escape from punishment; the negative particle min makes the denial comprehensive.

BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r5.claim: There is no viable denial of deeds because they are recorded and the limbs testify, even though people may verbally say they were not polytheists.

BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r6.speaker: الجنيد
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r6.claim: Junayd says the Real answers the person who hears His calls, commands, and address; one who hears such calls is already in the place to respond.

BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r7.claim: For ordinary people, answering means keeping the covenant, fulfilling God’s right, and turning from disobedience to obedience.

BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r8.claim: For the elite, answering means surrendering to pre-eternal decrees and turning from worldly ornaments and desires.

BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p259#4/r9.claim: For the most select lovers, it means sincere seeking, abandoning both worlds, and giving themselves to the divine presence in pursuit of union.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r1.claim: Respond to the Lord when the Messenger calls you to what brings salvation.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r10.claim: A possible active-participle sense is that no one distinguishes their conditions in order to show mercy, but al-Ālūsī calls this far-fetched.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r2.speaker: ابن ملك
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r2.claim: Ibn Malik allows min Allāh to attach to mard, treating the la-noun like a quasi-annexed noun and leaving it without tanwīn; the source adduces two parallels.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r3.claim: Another parse supplies an omitted demonstrative subject: the day is from God, as an independent answer to the question, from whom?

ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r4.claim: Other grammarians make the phrase circumstantial, attach it to the negation, or connect it to what the wording implies, comparing 68:2.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r5.claim: Attaching the phrase to yaʾtī is contrary to the apparent wording and sense; describing the day with it is also weak in meaning.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r6.claim: The apparent referent of the irreversible day is the Resurrection, rather than the day of death.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r7.claim: Maljaʾ can be a place noun meaning refuge or a verbal noun.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r8.claim: Nakir means denial as a verbal noun, irregularly formed; their denial that they were idolaters is treated as nothing because it cannot help against evidence and testimony of their limbs.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p52#2/r9.claim: Another explanation says there is no denial because circumstances and stations differ, so what they say in one state does not count as denial in another.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r1.claim: Istijābah means answering a caller; by extension it means obeying what the Prophet conveys from God, so people must obey before the Day of Judgment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r2.claim: The lām in li-rabbikum marks the recipient and strengthens transitivity; the underlying form is istajābahu lah, as in the construction in 2:186.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r3.speaker: كعب الغنوي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r3.claim: Kaʿb al-Ghanawī's couplet supplies poetic evidence for istajāba li, including the form lam yastajibhu.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r4.claim: Marrad is a verbal noun meaning return; ‘no return’ says the Day cannot be reversed. Min Allāh can attach to ‘comes’ or to the predicate, but not directly complete marrad, which would make lā's noun quasi-annexed and inflected rather than built on fatḥa.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p131/r5.claim: Maljaʾ literally means a refuge, but here it figuratively means a protector who can shield people from punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p132/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p132/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p132/r1.claim: Nakīr is a verbal noun: on that Day people will have no grounds to deny what they receive and can only acknowledge it.

TABATABAI:42:45-47/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:45-47/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:45-47/r8.claim: The command to answer the Lord is a summons and warning about the Resurrection, not merely about the day of death.

TABATABAI:42:45-47/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:45-47/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:45-47/r9.claim: The interpretation that the irreversible day means the day of death does not fit the context.

TABATABAI:42:47-49/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:47-49/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:47-49/r1.claim: The other grammatical analyses of the phrase are not useful enough to report.

TABATABAI:42:47-49/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:47-49/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:47-49/r2.claim: No refuge means nowhere to seek shelter from God, and no denial means they cannot deny their deeds once everything is exposed.

ASAD-NOTES:42:47#n47/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:47#n47/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:47#n47/r1.claim: The phrase literally says from God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p156/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p156/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p156/r4.claim: Verses 44–50 resume verse 36’s contrast between the opponents’ temporary worldly life and the believers’ lasting Hereafter reward; the believers’ traits make the glad tidings immediate for oppressed Muslims and foreshadow their success.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p156/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p156/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p156/r5.claim: The discourse resumes by assuring the Prophet that opponents subject to God’s law cannot be guided by anyone else and will realize this too late, then gives them a final chance to reform and explains their arrogance as ingratitude for God’s favors.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p159/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p159/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p159/r3.claim: In Islahi’s syntactic reading, “from God” connects to “arrives,” and “that cannot be put off” qualifies “day.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p159/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p159/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p159/r4.claim: The verse warns people that there is still time to answer their Lord, but when the certain Day arrives there will be no refuge or ability to reject what comes; they must submit.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p159/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p159/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p159/r5.claim: The word nakīr is better understood as rejecting something repulsive from a sense of honour, rather than as simple denial.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:44/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:44/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:44/r18.claim: The irreversible day may mean the day God will not reverse after decreeing it; commentators identify it as death or the Resurrection.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:44/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:44/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:44/r19.claim: Because nakir has several meanings, the closing phrase can mean no helper, no power to change the bad outcome, no dignity, or no denial of one's deeds.

STUDYQURAN:42:47/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r1.speaker: Bg, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r1.claim: One interpretation is to answer the person calling people to their Lord, believe in him, and follow him.

STUDYQURAN:42:47/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r2.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r2.claim: The caller referred to in that interpretation is the Prophet Muhammad.

STUDYQURAN:42:47/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r3.claim: Another interpretation is to respond to what calls people to God, such as faith and obedience.

STUDYQURAN:42:47/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r4.speaker: Qu
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r4.claim: Responding to God can also mean keeping the covenant with Him and observing His due.

STUDYQURAN:42:47/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r5.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r5.claim: The Judgment Day cannot be repelled or averted because once God's decree is made, He grants no further reprieve.

STUDYQURAN:42:47/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r6.claim: After the decree there is no opportunity for repentance or atonement, as the escape language of 75:10–12 illustrates.

STUDYQURAN:42:47/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r7.claim: The profligate and disbelievers will be unable to deny their condition and will admit their sins, as elsewhere described.

STUDYQURAN:42:47/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:47/r8.claim: The day may instead refer to the moment of death, meaning response and repentance remain possible until then.
